title: Weighted cohort synchronizer with delayed commit and self-heal
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces a cohort-weighted synchronizer runtime component that allows delayed commits for short-lived canaries and automated self-heal on metric regressions. Configurable parameters documented in rollout.md; default behavior is backwards compatible when the feature gate is off.
description: Motivation: Reduce noisy rollouts and minimize unsafe rapid commits during multi-cohort experiments by introducing a lightweight synchronizer that enforces weighted, delayed commits with an automated repair path. This PR implements a runtime controller and control-plane wiring to support: 1) delayed commit windows (configurable per-rollout), 2) cohort-weighted commit arbitration that respects session-affinity constraints, 3) self-heal workflows that automatically attempt a safe repair (redeploy+replay) when key SLOs breach during the commit delay, and 4) hooks for shadow-to-canary handoff and A/B bridged transitions. Summary of changes: - control plane: rollout API extended with 'commitDelayMs', 'weightSyncStrategy', and 'repairPolicy' fields, with validation and migration fallback; - runtime: new CohortSynchronizer component that coordinates multi-cohort commits using a lightweight lease and two-phase commit semantics across serving nodes; supports 'grace-split' where traffic is slowly shifted in micro-steps; - telemetry: rollout-trace spans, per-cohort metrics (pendingCommitRatio, repairAttempts), and aggregated SLI events emitted to observability; - QA: integration harness for simulating weighted cohorts, session-affine traffic, and network partitions; - docs: rollout.md and example manifests in examples/rollouts demonstrating typical canary->A/B->primary flows. Design notes: The synchronizer treats each cohort as a participant with a declared weight; during commit windows it computes a safe commit vector that respects both global capacity and session affinity constraints. Commits are delayed by default 30s (configurable) to let short transients settle; during the delay we run background samplers that evaluate latency, error-rate, and a lightweight quality signal (for models, a smoke-openai-eval) against the baseline. If thresholds breach, the repairPolicy may trigger one of: cancel (revert weights to pre-commit), soft-repair (redeploy new replica set with fallback model), or replay-repair (capture failing session samples for offline replay and auto-dismiss until operator review). Backwards compatibility: rollout API changes are opt-in via feature flag 'cohort_weight_sync_v1'. Existing rollouts without the new fields behave as before. Migration plan: - canary: opt-in small percentage rollouts for 2 weeks; - monitor: run nightly cohort-sim tests in perf-lab; - widen: enable the feature for internal customers, then gradual public rollout. Testing: unit tests for the synchronization protocol, e2e tests simulating cohort storms, and manual runbook for incident response included. Related: ENG-4512 (cohort orchestration refactor), ENG-4590 (observability schema updates). Checklist: - [x] API schema and validation - [x] runtime synchronizer implementation - [x] telemetry metrics and trace spans - [x] integration tests and perf lab scenarios - [x] docs and quickstart examples - [x] release notes drafted Rollout plan: merge behind feature flag, enable on canary org, monitor realtime SLIs (p95 latency, 5xx rate, model-quality smoke) for 48h, then increase exposure by powers-of-two with 1h holdpoints. Links: rollout.md in repo, Linear tasks ENG-4512/4590, perf lab job #perf-2026-02-14. This description is intentionally compact; see the changed files and comments for implementation details.

review_thread: Ravi Patel: Could you clarify how session affinity is preserved across micro-steps? We need a clear invariant here.
Maya Chen: The synchronizer tracks KV-based session keys and prefers stable routing; when micro-steps reassign weights it pins existing sessions for 'holdDurationMs' to avoid mid-session model swap.
Diego Castillo: Suggest adding a safety gate on cluster-wide CPU pressure to avoid commit during resource exhaustion.
Maya Chen: Added node pressure check; commit now fails fast with a diagnostic event (see lease_manager.go).
Asha Menon: Integration tests look good but one flaky test in cohort_protocol_test.go needs stabilization.

examples_snippet:
# example manifest for weighted cohort canary
apiVersion: rollout.redwood.io/v1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: weighted-cohort-canary
spec:
  commitDelayMs: 30000
  weightSyncStrategy: proportional
  repairPolicy: replay-repair
  cohorts:
    - name: control
      weight: 80
      selector: role=control
    - name: canary
      weight: 20
      selector: role=canary
  sessionAffinity:
    key: session_id
    holdDurationMs: 120000
